title: Robbers Cave (Sherif, 1954)

youtube.title: They Turned 22 Boys Into Enemies. Then This Fixed It #Shorts
youtube.description:
You're eleven, at a summer camp. You don't know another group of boys is camping across the woods.
Within days, the two groups are burning flags and raiding cabins.

This is Muzafer Sherif's 1954 Robbers Cave experiment, told from the inside. Competition turned two groups of boys into enemies. Just putting them together made it worse. What finally worked was a problem neither group could solve alone.

Who is YOUR other group, and what goal could you share? Tell me in the comments.

Sources:
- Sherif, M., Harvey, O. J., White, B. J., Hood, W. R., & Sherif, C. W. (1961). Intergroup Conflict and Cooperation: The Robbers Cave Experiment. University of Oklahoma Book Exchange.
- Sherif, M. (1958). Superordinate goals in the reduction of intergroup conflict. American Journal of Sociology, 63(4), 349-356.

#psychology #robberscave #groupconflict #shorts #mindset

sources: Sherif et al. (1954/1961), Intergroup Conflict and Cooperation: The Robbers Cave Experiment: 22 boys about 11-12 years old at Robbers Cave State Park, Oklahoma, in two groups (Eagles and Rattlers) who at first did not know of each other.

Same report: competitions (baseball, tug-of-war, treasure hunt, prizes for the winners) led to flag burning, cabin raids and name-calling; at the end of the competition stage about 93% of friendship choices were within the own group.

Same report: mere contact (meals, movies, fireworks) did not reduce hostility and meals turned into food fights; superordinate goals (a broken water supply, a stuck food truck pulled with the tug-of-war rope) did; the boys asked to go home together on one bus.
lines: You're eleven, at a summer camp in Oklahoma. You have no idea another group of boys is camping across the woods.
Nineteen fifty-four. Twenty-two boys, split into two groups. Yours names itself the Eagles. The others call themselves the Rattlers.
Then the counselors announce a contest. Baseball, tug of war, treasure hunts. Prizes for the winners. Nothing for the losers.
Within days, it turns ugly. Your group burns their flag. They raid your cabin, flip your beds and steal your stuff.
At the worst point, about ninety-three percent of every boy's friends came from his own group. The other side was the enemy.
So the researchers just put everyone together. Shared meals, movies, fireworks. It got worse. The meals turned into food fights.
Then the water supply breaks. The food truck gets stuck. So both groups grab the same rope and pull, together.
Meeting the enemy didn't end the hate. Needing them did. On the last day, they all asked to ride home on one bus.
Who is your other group? And what goal could you only reach together?
